items.rationale: Pipelining overlaps instructions, so more of them finish in a given time; one instruction still takes the same time.
The first instruction takes 4 cycles, and each of the other 99 finishes one cycle after the one before it: 4 + 99 = 103 cycles, against 400 without overlap.

items.answer: Instructions overlap, so one finishes every cycle even though each one still takes the same time.
accepted: Several instructions are in different stages at the same time
A new instruction starts before the earlier one finishes
items.rationale: A right answer says that instructions overlap, and that only the total gets shorter, not the time of one instruction.
